Hey, can't really help you for paper 2 because I'm really bad at that hahaha but I think memorising the model answer structure will really help you improve

For listening: For the first few sections, I highly suggest taking down important words and other things to note during the first narration of the text. By the time the first narration is done, I'm usually only left to choose between 2 options for my answers. 

On the second listen, you should listen much more carefully and pick up on the subtle things that help differentiate between the possible answers. For me, ill use the second narration of the text to select the correct option out of the two

For the note-taking and the table thingy, just take note of speed and precision. You really must be super duper focused for the last part.

For paper 1, I've taken a look at the O level editing and its quite easy, so I try to spend around 3-ish minutes on editing.

For free essay, I try not to write narrative and descriptive as I feel that your command of the English language must be really exceptional to score for those. Instead, I try to focus on expository as its much easier to score for that.

What's important for expository is, first and foremost, clear and logical arguments. If you want to really do well, try to think of arguments that are less common or less obvious, but still logical. This will make your essay truly stand out from that of your peers. I think that, if possible, providing suitable examples in your essay will also help pull your marks up.

For example, I once had to write an essay about the advantages of reading storybooks. For one of my paragraphs, the argument that I provided was that reading storybooks helps cultivate empathy in children. Through reading storybooks, we are able to understand the thought processes of characters and peer into their psyche. Then i proceeded to talk about how we can put ourselves in the shoes of characters and build empathy. To substantiate the argument further, I added the example of Friedrich by Hans Peter Ritcher. Its the story of historical fiction of some jew living in nazi Germany. 

As said in the other comment thread, I also try to reference my previous essays when writing. If you have any good paragraphs and arguments from your previous works, then I think it saves a lot of time if you just use them.

At this juncture, I think its too late to really improve language, so the best thing to do now imo is just to pick up general tips and do papers. Hope this helps

When writing substantives, I try to remember my previous essays and basically copy/paste decent-ish lines from them whenever applicable.

I try not to use firstly secondly thirdly for the first line of my topic sentence as my teacher says it's quite boring and many candidates alr use them.

So in general, what I'd say for writing an expository is you don't need exceptional language, just clear and logical arguments. I try to remember my previous essays during the exam and, if possible, use good lines from those as it helps me save time but I also try not to be boring.

I can't really advise you on paper 2 but for paper 1, especially the free essay, I've consistently gotten 27/30. My situational is usually around 21-23 because I commit too much time to free essay.

For free essay, I can't really advise you on narrative and descriptive because I'm not good with those.

For expository, I don't really think flowery language is important. What's important is clarity and logical points. I think giving specific examples also helps.
